messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming.latency.p99 > 5000ms in pool-3 (shared-gpu). SLO breaches detected for streaming endpoints. Auto-paged oncall. Incident ticket created: INC-3742.

Jules (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing initial metrics. p95 ~ 800ms, p99 ~ 5-6s on pool-3 for last 10m. Streaming stalls reported.

Alex Kim: seeing the same on dashboards. Error surface is `streaming_hang` (client-side disconnects). A few customers seeing partial audio chunks/timeouts.

Sanjeev Patel: can we confirm it's multi-tenant IO or NVMe saturated? last noisy-neighbor looked like heavy writeback. running iostat and `nvidia-smi dmon` now.

infra-bot: iostat summary (10s avg):
Device            r/s     w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  await
nvme0n1         12.0  1024.1  2560  98304   12.8

Jules (oncall): blkio: several hosts in pool-3 showing `blkio.throttled_time` jumps. cgroup blkio.weight seems default.

Alex Kim: stack traces show long waits in `nvme_pci` vendor driver + stalled token flush in runtime. Also large KV cache checkpoints hitting disk on tenant-42.

Sanjeev Patel: confirmed tenant-42 doing large background checkpoint/flush to local NVMe -> burst writes ~100MB/s on single host, causing queue depth bump and streaming tail spikes for co-located tenants.

Jules (oncall): customer impact: 2 paying customers with streaming features degraded (CS notified). marking severity: Sev2 (degraded service, sustained high p99).

Priya Rao (CS): I have the two customers on standby. will send an initial heads-up and offer degraded fallback.

Alex Kim: immediate mitigations proposal:
- throttle tenant-42 IO via cgroup blkio throttle (soft limit)
- migrate tenant-42 off the busiest host(s) (live migrate containers)
- enable per-tenant streaming fallback to CPU-hosted smaller model for critical request paths
- temporarily increase pool-3 NVMe iops QoS if we can from infra

Sanjeev Patel: runbook steps: 
```
# identify top writers
sudo cgget -r blkio.throttle.read_bps_device /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenants/tenant-42
# apply throttle (example)
echo "8:0 10485760" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenants/tenant-42/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
# live migrate container
kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data pod/noisy-tenant-42-*
```

Jules (oncall): I'm going to apply a conservative write_bps (10MB/s) to tenant-42 now and trigger a migration. will run in 60s.

infra-bot: applied `blkio.throttle.write_bps_device=8:0 10485760` to tenant-42 on host gpu-3b.

Evan Li: after throttle, p99 dropped from ~5.5s -> 1.2s in 90s. p95 back to ~520ms. streaming stalls still present but much reduced.

Alex Kim: good signal. need a longer-term fix: tenant isolation (move heavy checkpoints to dedicated pool) + autoscale eviction runbook. open ticket RFC for tenant QoS.

Priya Rao (CS): Notifying affected customers: sent initial message: "We're investigating a streaming degradation; we've applied mitigations and will follow up with ETA. No data loss."

Jules (oncall): setting incident command: Jules = IC, Alex = Mitigation lead, Sanjeev = Infra lead, Priya = Customer liaison. changing channel to #incidents-3742 for focused comms.

Sanjeev Patel: follow-ups I will do:
- sweep autoscaler logs to see if tenant-42's checkpointing was triggered by internal GC
- check kernel `blk_cgroup` counters and NVMe SMART for requeue errors
- plan migration window to Dedicated pool-2 for tenant-42 (low-risk window in 30m)

Alex Kim: add an automated fallback route in runtime config for streaming requests when p99 > 1500ms: route to smaller quantized model (q4) so clients keep a streaming experience. quick patch queued.

Jules (oncall): incident status: mitigation applied, p99 improved but still above SLO borderline. continuing live migration. ETA for return to normal: 35-45m.

Incident Bot: Handoff reminder: please populate `INC-3742` ticket with timeline and action items. Postmortem required.

Evan Li: note: observed a related but separate host (gpu-3d) with heavy writeback scheduled by nightly compaction. we'll sync compaction windows to avoid overlap.

Priya Rao (CS): customers acknowledged and appreciate quick mitigation. will follow up with postmortem summary once available.

Jules (oncall): I'll escalate to Eng Platform if migration stalls. leaving a running checklist in ticket:
- [x] apply cgroup throttle
- [x] migrate noisy tenant off host gpu-3b
- [ ] adjust checkpoint cadence for tenant-42
- [ ] postmortem + tuning: per-tenant IO budgets, autoscale heuristics, compaction windows

Alex Kim: after migration completes, we should consider a short-term patch to runtime to detect large sequential writes from KV checkpoints and stagger them across hosts.

Sanjeev Patel: taking ownership of the RCA. I'll include kernel cgroup counters, NVMe stats, and tenant workload pattern.

Jules (oncall): last update: migration finished at +28m, p99 stabilized ~480-520ms, p95 ~400ms. marking incident as mitigated. will keep thread open for follow-ups and postmortem assignment. :white_check_mark:

Priya Rao (CS): customers now reporting recovered experience. closing customer comms loop.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-3742 status -> MITIGATED. Please file postmortem in 48h.

Evan Li: adding note: add metrics alert for blkio.throttled_time increase per-host (to catch early).

Alex Kim: thanks team. postmortem owners: Sanjeev (RCA), Alex (runtime fix), Jules (runbook updates), Priya (customer summary).

Jules (oncall): handing off to follow-up rotation. oncall clear in 10m.

(End of thread)
